about: A workflow every account can find and run: find the short-video formats that already sell apps like yours, rebuild the best three around your one best feature, and test them against a downloads-per-1,000-views bar. One workflow-recipe row in the shape of the shared recipe shelf (job, input_schema, ordered steps, each with do, submit and checks).

payload.produces: Each Monday: the formats winning in the niche this week, scored, with 3 new scripts for the best one; the ranked formats are a "what is working now" post.
payload.label: Find and test the short-video formats that sell your app
payload.job: Map which short-video formats won in the person's category over the last 30 and 90 days, read the 8 most relevant videos in detail, score the formats and pick the top 3, write 9 scripts (3 per format, 3 hooks each, the app on screen by 0:03) that keep each format's structure and change every word, list the creators who already posted for the person's competitors, then plan a 2-week test of 3 videos per format and end every format that gets under 5 downloads per 1,000 views. Every number comes from a tool call or from the person's own analytics; where there is none, the answer is "no data". The AI drafts, the person approves the exact scripts, films and posts: the AI never posts by itself.

source.author: Jake Castillo and a second X author on the same method
source.name: Jake Castillo, X post of 2026-10-30, and a second X post (https://x.com/fuckgrowth/status/2114783239705424235): a research library of viral UGC videos plus an agent prompt that turns it into a content plan
source.note: Their claims, not checked here: after about 25 videos from the last 30 days, 3 or 4 formats keep winning; a format a brand re-runs about 20 times is probably making money (a guess, labelled as one in this workflow); a good format shows the app's value within 3 to 5 seconds; the bar to keep a format is 5 downloads per 1,000 views. The method: map the niche, copy the structure and not the words, make 3 to 5 hooks per structure, use the creators who already posted for competitors as the outreach list, and every week add new winners, run 10 fresh tests, move the best organic videos to paid, and keep a log of which borrowed formats converted for the person's own app. The strategist prompt asks for every number from the library tool, "no data" instead of an invented number, formats scored 1 to 5 on reach, momentum, fit with the moment the app shows its value, ease to film and proof from competitors, and a Monday rerun checklist. The video library is DarkUGC (darkugc.com), a free library; its connector needs a free account of the person's own, its terms forbid scraping, bulk download and training models on it, and they allow quoting short parts with a link. This workflow uses it only through the person's own signed-in connector, one request at a time, and keeps nothing but short notes and links.

app.description: The person's app, in one plain sentence: what it is and who it is for

best_feature.description: The one feature that shows the app's value fastest on a phone screen

category.description: The app's category in the person's own words, for example language learning or period tracking

competitors.description: Up to 5 competing apps, by name as people know them

library.description: darkugc-connector when the person has connected their free DarkUGC account (tools search_videos, get_video, analyze_brand, analyze_niche, find_creators, get_creator, query_library, top_hooks, trending_now, get_search_filters); own-tools to use public video addresses with yt-dlp metadata and the person's own outlier scoring instead. If left out, use darkugc-connector when its tools are listed and own-tools when they are not.

steps.title: Match the category, competitors and formats to the library's own names
steps.do: Decide the data route: if the DarkUGC connector tools are listed for you (get_search_filters, analyze_niche, analyze_brand, top_hooks, trending_now, get_video, find_creators, get_creator), the route is darkugc-connector; otherwise it is own-tools. If the input library says otherwise, follow the input. On the darkugc-connector route call get_search_filters once and copy, exactly as it lists them, the category name, one brand name for each competitor, and the format names that fit the category. A competitor the library does not list goes in competitors_missing; never guess a name. If a tool answers that the person must sign in or has reached a daily limit, call tool:tell-the-person with { "title": "Connect your DarkUGC account", "body": "The free DarkUGC connector needs your own account. Add https://darkugc.com/mcp as a connector, sign in, and tell me when it is done. If you would rather not, say so and I will use public video addresses instead." } and wait; do not make an account for the person and do not use another way into the library. On the own-tools route, matched_names stay empty and each competitor is described by the public profile address the person gives you for it (ask with tool:tell-the-person if you have none).

category_name.description: The category exactly as the library names it, or the input category on the own-tools route

competitors_matched.description: Competitor names exactly as the library lists them (or the profile address on the own-tools route)

competitors_missing.description: Competitors from the input that the library does not list

format_names.description: Format names exactly as the library lists them, empty on the own-tools route

checks.says: Only the person's competitors can be missing

steps.title: Map the niche: what won in the last 30 and 90 days
steps.do: On the darkugc-connector route: call analyze_niche for the category over the last 90 days and again over the last 30 days; call analyze_brand once for each matched competitor; call top_hooks for the category; call trending_now for the last 14 days. Copy every figure exactly as the tool returned it, with the tool name and the window it covered. On the own-tools route: for each public profile address from the previous step, use the tool tool:github:yt-dlp-yt-dlp to read metadata only (for example `yt-dlp --flat-playlist --dump-json <profile address>`), which lists each video's address, title, upload date and view count; do not download the videos. Keep the last 30 days, and mark a video an outlier when its views are at least 5 times the median views of its own profile and at least 10,000 (score every video against the median of the profile it came from, never against all profiles together). Then read the outliers and name the formats you can see in them in plain words. In both routes, for every claim write the measure and where it came from; a figure no tool gave you is not written, and a question no tool answers is answered "no data". Write at most 25 videos into top_videos, the ones the data ranks highest, each with its address, the platform, the recorded views and the post date. Write 3 or 4 formats that keep winning, each with how many of the videos it covers, its typical hook in your words, how the app shows up, and the call to action. Do not call a format a winner from fewer than 3 videos. Add rerun_guess for a brand that ran one format about 20 times or more, and write the words "a guess, not a measured result" in it.

source.description: The tool name, or yt-dlp metadata read of which profile
The tool call or metadata read this format came from

rerun_guess.description: Only when a brand re-ran this format about 20 times or more; must say it is a guess

no_data.description: Every question you asked that no tool could answer

checks.says: At least one winning format was found
At least 8 different videos were read, enough to pick the 8 most relevant
A re-run count is never written as proof of earnings

steps.title: Read the 8 most relevant videos in detail
steps.do: From top_videos pick the 8 most relevant to the person's app and best_feature (a video whose viewer has the same problem the feature solves ranks above one that only has more views); say in why_chosen what made each relevant. On the darkugc-connector route call get_video for each of the 8 and copy from its answer. On the own-tools route open each video's public page with tool:read-a-page-in-my-browser (or read its yt-dlp metadata and caption text) and note only what you can see or read. For each video record: the hook (the first line or first visible move), the structure as 3 to 6 plain beats in order, the second at which the app first appears on screen (a number of seconds; if the tool does not say and you cannot see it, write null and put the video in no_data), the call to action, a script template with the words replaced by slots like <problem> or <feature result>, and the link. Do not copy a video's spoken words into the template: slots only. Record a short quote of the hook only if it is under 15 words and keep its link next to it.

checks.says: Every video read was one of the mapped videos

steps.title: Score the formats 1 to 5 and pick the top 3
steps.do: Score each winning format from the map-niche step on five measures, a whole number from 1 to 5 each, and give in one sentence for each score the evidence behind it: reach (how many recorded views its videos had), momentum (whether it grew in the last 30 days compared with the 90-day window, from the figures you recorded), aha_fit (how fast the person's best_feature can show its value to a viewer: 5 means the feature is on screen and its result visible within 3 seconds), ease_to_film (what the person needs to film it with a phone and no crew) and competitor_proof (how many of the competitors' videos use it). Where the evidence for a score is "no data", score it 1 and say "no data"; never raise a score without evidence. Add the total. A format whose videos only show the app's value after 5 seconds, or never, is marked slow_value: true and can be picked only if fewer than 3 formats are not slow. Pick the 3 with the highest totals; on a tie prefer the higher aha_fit. Show the person the table and the three picked.

evidence.description: One sentence per score, with the figure or the words no data

steps.title: Write 9 scripts: 3 per format, 3 hooks each, the app on screen by 0:03
steps.do: For each picked format write up to 3 scripts (9 scripts in all when 3 formats are picked; fewer formats means fewer scripts, never padding), each built around the person's best_feature and nothing else. Each script keeps the structure (the beats, in order) of the videos of that format from the read-videos step, and changes every word: no sentence, line or caption may be copied from any video you read. Give each script 3 hooks (different openings, not one hook reworded), the beats with seconds, the shot list a person can film on a phone, the on-screen text, and the call to action. The app must be on screen with the feature visible by second 3: set app_on_screen_by_second to the second in your timing (3 or less) and make beat 1 show it. State only what the person told you about the app; do not write a number, result, review or testimonial the person did not give you. If the script shows another person, the person must really have that experience or the script says it is a portrayal. Put in notes anything the person must supply before filming.

checks.says: Scripts are written only for the picked formats
Every picked format has at least one script
No unproven claim in a hook

steps.title: List the creators who already posted for the competitors
steps.do: On the darkugc-connector route call find_creators filtered to each matched competitor over the last 90 days, keep the 15 with the most recorded views for those competitors (fewer if the tool returns fewer; never fill the list), then call get_creator for the top 5 and copy their brands, views, posting rhythm, formats and best videos. On the own-tools route list the accounts that posted the outlier videos from the map-niche step, from their public pages. Record each creator with the profile address the tool gives, the competitors they posted for, and their recorded views. Use this list only to ask the creators, one person at a time and in the person's own words, whether they would make a video; do not copy it out into a separate database, do not message anyone yourself, and do not scrape profile pages.

checks.says: Each creator is listed for a competitor the person named
The five detailed creators come from the list

steps.title: The person approves the exact scripts
steps.do: Show the person, in the chat, each script exactly as it would be filmed: title, the 3 hooks, the beats with seconds, the shot list, the call to action and the notes. Ask for each: "Do you approve this script exactly as written?" Wait. Ask also which scripts they can film in the next 2 weeks; choose none for them. If they change a word, make only that change, show the whole script again and ask again. Copy their approving answer exactly into approval_words and copy each approved script's title unchanged. Nothing is filmed or posted in this step.

approval_words.description: The person's own words approving this exact script

checks.says: Each approved script is a drafted script, unchanged

steps.title: Plan a 2-week test: 3 videos per format, with a stop bar
steps.do: Plan the test from the approved scripts: 3 videos for each picked format that has approved scripts (a format with fewer approved scripts gets fewer videos, never a script that was not approved), spread over 2 weeks, each on a posting date the person chooses. State the stop bar before anything is posted: a format whose videos have fewer than 5 downloads per 1,000 views after the person's measuring window (default 7 days after posting) is dropped, and 5 or more is kept (this bar is the original author's, and the person may set a different bar now, before posting, and write it in stop_bar_per_1000_views). Say where the person reads downloads and views (the app store or attribution dashboard for downloads, the platform's analytics for views) and what link or code ties a download to a video; if the person has no way to tie downloads to a video, say so in tracking_gap and do not invent one. The person films and posts; you do not.

tracking.description: Where downloads and views are read, and what ties a download to a video

tracking_gap.description: none, or what cannot be measured yet

steps.title: Set the weekly rerun and the log that becomes the playbook
steps.do: Write the Monday checklist the person will run each week, as 5 steps in this order, each naming the exact tool or page: (1) read trending_now and the last 7 days of analyze_niche (or, on the own-tools route, re-read the competitor profiles' metadata and outliers) and list the new winners; (2) write down which of last week's videos reached the stop bar, with their downloads per 1,000 views from the person's own analytics; (3) choose 10 fresh tests built from the new winners and the kept formats, as new scripts to approve; (4) pick the best organic videos by downloads per 1,000 views to run as paid, only with the person's approval of any spend; (5) append to the log one row per borrowed format: the format, the videos made, views, downloads, downloads per 1,000 views, and kept or dropped. The log starts empty; every number in it is from the person's analytics and none is estimated. The log is the playbook for this app, and it is the person's data.

first_review_date.description: The first Monday after the test's measuring window ends
